key_insight: RoboTTT shows that robot policies can use extremely long visuomotor context—up to 8K timesteps—without increasing inference latency. This enables new behaviors like one-shot imitation from human videos and real-time on-the-fly policy improvement.
problem_solved: Most robot foundation models can only use short histories, which limits their ability to learn from demonstrations, adapt during deployment, and handle long-horizon tasks or changing conditions.
method: Introduces Test-Time-Training Robot Policies (RoboTTT), a model and training recipe designed to scale visuomotor context length dramatically.
Uses long-context training so the policy can condition on up to 8K timesteps of robot and visual history.
Preserves inference speed by structuring the approach so longer context does not increase runtime latency.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path to more adaptable robot policies that can learn from fewer examples and improve during use. It expands the frontier of what foundation models can do in robotics without sacrificing responsiveness.

paper_title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yunfan Jiang, Yevgen Chebotar, Ruijie Zheng, Fengyuan Hu, Yunhao Ge
